chunks: He said: Sulaiman ibn Dawood narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Basir that he said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:

In the master of this affair are four practices from four prophets; a practice from Musa, a practice from Isa, a practice from Yusuf, and a practice from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). As for from Musa, he is fearful and anticipating; as for from Yusuf, it is prison; as for from Isa, it is said: he died, yet he did not die; and as for from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), it is the sword.
ai.seo_question: What are the four prophetic similarities in the state of the Imam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines the four essential states of the Imam during the period of occultation, linking them to the trials of Prophets Musa, Yusuf, Isa, and Muhammad (peace be upon them). It highlights the theological concept of the Imam's hidden presence and readiness, balancing spiritual vigilance with the potential for political action, thereby refuting the Waqifiya who denied the Imam's continued authority.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 57 - Sulaiman bin Dawood has narrated from Ali bin Abil Hamza from Abu Basir that he said: I heard Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) say:

In the master of this affair [Imamate] are present four similarities from the practices of the prophets. A similarity with Musa bin Imran (a.s), a similarity with Isa bin Maryam (a.s), a similarity with Prophet Yusuf (a.s) and also a similarity with Prophet Muhammad (s). The similarity with Musa (a.s) is fear and anticipation; similarity with Yusuf is prison, similarity with Isa (a.s) is that it would be said with regard to him that he is dead; whereas he is alive and present; and finally a similarity with the Prophet of Islam (s), which is that he would stage an armed uprising.
